sources.title: Buffalo Lake, sheet 85B, Land Use Information Series
sources.agency: Lands Directorate, Environmental Management Service, Department of the Environment, Canada; hosted by Agriculture and Agri-Food Canada
sources.publication_date_basis: Year printed in original bottom imprint
sources.source_kind: Original government thematic cartographic sheet, inspected as raster
sources.source_scope_preflight: Distinct federal land-use map, not a gazetteer or naming-register record.
own_factual_extraction: The printed frame spans 116–114°W and 60–61°N. Scale is 1:250,000; the sheet states Transverse Mercator and North American Datum 1927.
The name is printed across the complete large basin in the southwest quadrant, whose broad western arm, northeastern head and south-projecting lobe correspond to the complete target polygon.
The adjoining-sheet inset locates Buffalo Lake on 85B and Tathlina Lake on 85C to the west.
sources.map_coverage: Complete target basin and adjacent smaller waters; Great Slave Lake and Hay River supply northern/western context.
sources.registration: Manual visual comparison against printed geographic graticule, complete geometry coordinates and distinctive outline; no fitted raster transformation or residual-error calculation. Historical datum differs from modern source coordinates.
sources.evidence_limit: Historical mapped name and generalized basin identity; no present-day cadastral/survey shoreline or formal naming decision is established.

sources.title: Northwest Territories Oil and Gas Annual Report 2023, Figure 5: Cameron Hills Land Disposition Map
sources.agency: Government of the Northwest Territories, Industry, Tourism and Investment, Mineral and Petroleum Resources Division
sources.date_detail: Map document filename printed on figure contains Mar6_2024; PDF creation metadata is 2024-09-17T16:15:02Z. These are production metadata, not a confirmed publication date.
sources.source_kind: Original government annual report and regional map, page 15 (PDF page 15)
sources.source_scope_preflight: Distinct territorial petroleum report and map, not a geographical-name register.
own_factual_extraction: Tathlina is shown between 118°W and 117°W near 60°30′N, west of Enterprise; the target polygon lies east of 116°W.
Kakisa Lake is north of Tathlina. Buffalo Lake appears east/southeast of Enterprise, but its eastern portion is cut by the map frame.
Figure metadata states WGS84 and a modified Lambert conformal conic projection.
sources.map_coverage: Cameron Hills region, both candidate names and nearby lakes; Buffalo basin only partially covered.
sources.registration: Printed meridians and parallels used for regional disambiguation only.
sources.evidence_limit: Independently excludes Tathlina geographically; cannot alone prove the full Buffalo perimeter because coverage is clipped.

sources.title: Bison Control Area Program: Annual Report of Survey Activities, November 2006–April 2007, Manuscript Report No. 216
sources.agency: Government of the Northwest Territories, Environment and Natural Resources
sources.source_kind: Original government wildlife-survey report, Figure 2 on printed page 6 (PDF page 11); supplementary regional panels on printed page 49 (PDF page 54)
sources.source_scope_preflight: Distinct wildlife surveillance report, not a gazetteer or naming publication.
own_factual_extraction: The regional map labels Buffalo Lake east of Enterprise and southeast of Hay River, beside Wood Buffalo National Park; Tathlina is separately labeled west of Enterprise and south of Kakisa.
The full named Buffalo basin is visible with a westward arm, northeastern head and southern lobe. The companion regional panel repeats the two distinct lake labels.
sources.map_coverage: Broad southern Northwest Territories overview includes Great Slave, Kakisa, Tathlina, Buffalo, Trout and Bistcho lakes.
sources.registration: Relative regional placement and whole-basin outline comparison; Figure 2 has no readable geographic graticule, so it is not the numerical registration source.
sources.evidence_limit: Corroborates regional identity; thematic small-scale map does not validate precise shorelines or island exclusions.

independence: Three separately published official thematic originals from two government jurisdictions. Common upstream base hydrography is possible; independent shoreline surveys are not claimed.
observation_method: Actual original images/PDF pages were downloaded and visually inspected using complete-page previews and readable detail crops; discovery snippets were not used as proof.

copyright_handling.published_content: Own factual extraction, brief map-name quotations, official URLs, retrieval timestamps, byte counts and SHA-256 hashes.
